text:
alex: quick idea — routing feels brittle when capacity is heterogeneous (A100 pools + L4 burst + CPU fallback). tenants with reserved capacity keep getting routed to cold L4s during spikes and we eat tail-latency/cost. proposal: attach a tiny per-request "budget" hint and surface per-tenant capacity profiles into the policy engine so decisions can prefer warm reserved pools or cheaper cold lanes based on a request budget. thoughts?

maria: curious — where does the budget come from? product/SDK or computed at edge?

alex: either. default could be inferred from route (e.g., high_priority routes -> budget=high). SDK can set `X-Redwood-Budget: low|med|high`. runtime can override with tenant quotas.

tom: +1 to explicit hinting. but we should keep scoring pure. i.e., scorer returns cost/latency estimates, admission layer consumes budget + quotas and makes binary accept/route decisions. separates concerns and keeps simulator consistent.
sophie: agree with separation. also we need a shadow-sim mode to validate routing shifts before rollouts. we can replay a day's traffic w/ new budget logic and measure tail latency + cost delta.
ryan: don't forget SLOs — budget hints must be bounded by SLA. e.g., budget=low can't be used to push below latency SLO for a tenant. fallback chain should encode SLO overrides.
irene: worried about head-of-line / priority inversion. if we prefer warm GPUs for high budget, low-budget requests might pile on cold GPUs and amplify tails. we need admission windows and backpressure signals.

alex: good call. propose adding two guardrails: 1) per-shard `max_low_budget_inflight` and 2) soft-token bucket for budgeted bypass that is replenished by successful quick completions.

(snip) example header and tiny policy sketch:

```
# request header
X-Redwood-Budget: low
X-Redwood-Tenant: acme

# pseudo policy (evaluator returns tags only)
if tenant.has_reserved_gpu and tenant.slo_ok then prefer: warm_reserved
else if budget == high then prefer: warm_burst
else prefer: cold_cheapest
```

maria: how would this interact with our current policy adapters? we have sidecar-based adapters and some library-inlined adapters. mixing runtime hints with adapters could be messy.

tom: adapter contract idea: scorer returns a small JSON blob {score, est_p95_ms, est_cost_unit}, admission layer consumes blob + hint. keep adapter surface stable. adapters only need to add est_* fields.
sophie: for rollout: 1) simulation + replay 2) shadow routing toggles in canary 3) incremental `max_low_budget_inflight` relax. also add alerting on queueing_iat and tail_latency per device class.

dev-bot: deploybot: canary cluster created for alex/budget-proto (cluster: routing-shadow-03) :rocket:

ryan: once canary runs, we should compute per-tenant deltas: cost/unit, p95, p99. if cost down but p99 up for >1% of requests, auto-roll back.
irene: also add fairness metric: fraction_of_served_from_reserved_by_tenant so we don't starve low-tier tenants on reserved capacity.

alex: ok next steps I'll draft a short RFC capturing: header proto, adapter contract change (est_* fields), admission token design, rollout plan + simulation checklist. assigning to myself — will ping for reviews. :thumbsup:

maria: lgtm, please include the data we need from telemetry (per-device inflight, queue_sz, avg_serv_time by budget).
alex: will do — thanks everyone.
